covers_slices: Slices 1-7 plus the naming pass, pages 1-8. THE CLASSIFICATION IS COMPLETE for 433-A(OIC): every bound key on the form is covered by exactly one entry, and adapters/hubspot/derive-names-433aoi.mjs CHECKS that against the map rather than this file asserting it.
_what_this_is: THE CROSSWALK CLASSIFICATION, AS DATA. For each correspondence between a 433-A(OIC) binding and its nearest 433-A counterpart, WHICH KIND of correspondence it is. Six slices of this classification existed only inside chat reports, which are the one artefact no sweep can reach - and a classification that lives in a report is re-derived from six reports by whoever does the provisioning pass, which is the retyped-count defect with more steps and worse inputs.
_this_binds_NOTHING: NO CROSSWALK BINDINGS. No HubSpot property is named, no canonical column is claimed, no map key is repointed. Every entry is a statement about how two PRINTED FORMS relate, and the provisioning pass reads it as INPUT to a decision rather than as the decision. That separation is the standing plan and this file does not move it. `oic` names a key in 433aoi.map.json and `a433` a key in 433a.map.json, both so a reader can go and look; naming a key is not binding it to anything.

_the_categories.exact: The same fact, computed the same way, in the same shape. A 433-A record's value for `a433` is the value 433-A(OIC) wants at `oic`, with no transformation. This is the only category a provisioning pass may reuse a property for without a decision.
_the_categories.superset: The OIC line asks for MORE than the 433-A line. A 433-A value is a correct partial answer and an incomplete one, so reusing it silently understates the OIC figure. Direction matters and is always OIC-broader here; the reverse is `asymmetric-the-other-way`.
_the_categories.different-arithmetic-same-name: The captions correspond and the ARITHMETIC does not. This is the most dangerous category on the form, because the names invite reuse and the resulting figure is wrong on a statement signed under penalty of perjury while every printed total still reconciles.
_the_categories.different-shape: The same facts, laid out differently - a different number of printed rows, a different grouping, a different overflow rule. The facts transfer; the container does not.
_the_categories.same-fact-different-decomposition: One quantity split into different parts by the two forms. Neither side is wrong and no line-to-line mapping exists: the crosswalk is per FACT, not per line, and going either way needs arithmetic the taxpayer signs for.
_the_categories.new: 433-A(OIC) prints it and 433-A prints nothing like it. Nothing to crosswalk; either intake or computation, and which one is a decision.
_the_categories.asymmetric-the-other-way: 433-A prints it and 433-A(OIC) does not. Recorded because a crosswalk read in one direction hides these entirely, and a 433-A fact with nowhere to go on the OIC form is a fact the OIC filing drops.

_why_the_offset_is_not_a_category: The expectation this crosswalk was opened to test - that 433-A(OIC) reuses the 433-A map with a +3 expense-line offset - HOLDS FOR THIRTEEN CONSECUTIVE EXPENSE LINES AND FOR NOTHING ELSE. It is recorded per entry below rather than as a rule, because two of the thirteen are not `exact` and the fourteenth 433-A line has no OIC line at all. An offset that is right thirteen times and wrong three ways is an authoring aid, not a function.

THE QUICK-SALE DISCOUNT. 433-A(OIC) prints 'X .8' against the retirement market value and 433-A prints no column of that kind anywhere on the form. A 433-A market value copied into (3a) overstates the OIC figure by 25% of what the OIC form actually wants, and every printed total on the page still reconciles. The attachment line (3b) carries the discount in its own caption too, where nothing can enforce it.

ONE printed row against 433-A's three, and the OIC attachment block splits into two cells - a total and a separate loan-balance figure - where the printed row carries its own 'Minus loan balance'. A taxpayer with two policies has one printed row and an attachment on this form.

Both forms ask the same six digital-asset facts, including the self-hosted wallet address. 433-A prints four rows and the OIC form prints one block, but the FACTS are identical and none is discounted - the digital-asset cells carry no 'X .8'.
The quick-sale discount again, on real property, plus two printed rows against three. A 433-A current market value is not the OIC figure - X-07's reasoning, on the largest numbers on the form.

Quick-sale discount, two rows against three, AND a printed lease/own conditional that zeroes the row - 'if the vehicle is leased, enter 0 as the total value'. 433-A asks for lease and ownership facts but never zeroes an equity figure on them.

THE VEHICLE EQUITY ALLOWANCE. The OIC form subtracts a printed $3,450 per vehicle on a joint offer and 433-A grants no such allowance anywhere. Nothing to crosswalk. The selector - whether the offer is joint - is on Form 656 and on no cell of this form, which is why (6d) is declared not checkable.

The OIC form asks whether the real property is for sale and at what listing price. 433-A asks neither. It is one question about the taxpayer's property as a whole rather than about either printed row, which is why it is bound as scalars and not as a group column.

entries.why: Two printed rows on both forms, but the OIC form adds an attachment roll-up and a full business DIGITAL-ASSET block - the same six facts as the personal block at (2c), asked again for the business. 433-A asks for business digital assets nowhere. THE GLOB IS GONE AND WHAT IT SWEPT IS ON THE RECORD. This entry wrote `8c_* digital-asset block` and its own prose named SIX facts; the prefix matched EIGHT keys. The two nobody named are 8c_total_digital_assets, which is a TOTAL rather than a fact of the block, and 8c_digital_asset_held, which is the CHECKBOX that gates the block - neither is one of the "same six facts as the personal block at (2c)" the prose claimed, and neither was ever looked at as a classified cell. Both are now spelled out and are classified different-shape along with the rest of this entry, which is a claim about them somebody can now disagree with. A glob is a blanket: it makes a claim over a set its author never enumerated, and the two cells it quietly carried are exactly what that costs.

Two printed rows on both, and the OIC rows carry the quick-sale discount that 433-A's do not. They also carry a printed conditional with NO selector on this form - 'if leased or used in the production of income, enter 0 as the total value' - where the page-3 vehicle rows at least print their own lease/own boxes. See map._table_or_scalars C-08 for why these two are one group and (7a)/(7b) are not.

The IRS-allowed deduction for professional books and tools of trade, subtracted from business assets. 433-A grants no such deduction. It is a PUBLISHED IRS FIGURE this repo does not hold, so nothing auto-fills it and the review page carries an advisory saying so.
BOX B, the business half of X-15. Computation.

entries.a433: 433-A Section 6 business income lines 68, 69, 70, 71 and the line 77 total

NARROWED from five sources; see _superseded_verbatim.

_superseded_verbatim.why: Five business income sources and their total, asked identically on both forms.

entries._what_it_got_right: That (12) through (15) and the (17) total are the same questions and the same arithmetic as 433-A lines 68-71 and 77.
entries._what_it_got_wrong: That all five sources are asked identically. 433-A splits its fifth source into line 72 "Cash Receipts not included in lines 68-71" AND four "Other Income (Specify below)" description/amount pairs at lines 73-76; 433-A(OIC) asks one plain "Other income" cell at (16). Five 433-A cells against one. Split out as X-80.

entries.why: Nine business expense lines. The line NUMBERS differ and the captions and the arithmetic do not. NARROWED from eleven lines plus the total; see _superseded_verbatim.

_superseded_verbatim.why: Eleven business expense lines and their total. The line NUMBERS differ and the captions and the arithmetic do not.

entries._what_it_got_right: That nine of the eleven printed expense lines are the same question and the same arithmetic under a different printed line number.
entries._what_it_got_wrong: Two of the eleven, and the total. (24) is printed "Vehicle costs (gas, oil, repairs, maintenance)" - ONE line over what 433-A splits into line 84 Vehicle Gasoline/Oil and line 85 Repairs and Maintenance. (27) is printed "Secured debts (not credit cards)" and 433-A prints no secured-debt line in its business expense block at all. And because (29) adds (27), the (29) total and 433-A line 89 are over different operand sets and can differ for one taxpayer at one moment. Split out as X-78, X-79 and X-81.

entries.why: BOX C, business income minus business expenses. 433-A computes a net business income figure on its income side (line 24) but prints no box here; the OIC form computes it in Section 6 and CARRIES IT ACROSS to page 6. See X-30 for what happens to it there.

THE OIC FORM ASKS ONLY WHETHER THEY EXIST. Two yes/no pairs against 433-A's five-row itemised table of notes and accounts receivable. A 433-A record carrying five receivable rows collapses to two booleans here, and the detail has nowhere to go on this form.

THE SAME FACTS, TRANSPOSED. 433-A splits taxpayer and spouse into separate LINES and groups by income TYPE; the OIC form splits them into separate ROWS of a four-across grid and groups by PERSON, then asks for a per-person total 433-A never computes. Every individual fact crosswalks; no LINE does. And the two forms disagree on how many 'other income' facts exist per person: 433-A prints two description/amount pairs shared across the household, the OIC grid prints one 'Other income' cell per person.

Interest and dividends on both. The OIC caption adds 'and royalties', which is a broadening in wording that the 433-A line's own instructions already cover; recorded as exact and flagged here rather than as a superset. THE LEAF NAME IS THE TRAP, NOT THE CROSSWALK: three widgets on this page are named Interest_Dividends and only this one is interest and dividends.
Distributions from K-1, IRA and similar. The same fact on both forms.
Net rental income, same fact both forms.

THE CAPTION NAMES A PRINTED CELL AND THEN INSTRUCTS THE PREPARER TO MAKE IT DIFFER. The OIC line reads 'Net business income from Box C' followed by '[Deductions for non-cash expenses on Schedule C (e.g., depreciation, depletion, etc.) are not permitted as an expense for offer purposes and must be added back in]'. A 433-A net business income computed from a Schedule C that deducted depreciation is NOT this figure and is smaller than it, so copying it understates household income, understates Box F and understates the offer. It is the clearest same-name-different-arithmetic pair on the form and the one most likely to be reused without thinking, because both captions say net business income.
Child support received. Same fact.
Alimony received. Same fact.

'Additional sources of income used to support the household, e.g., non-liable spouse, or anyone else who may contribute', with its own list cell. THIRD-PARTY CONTRIBUTIONS, which is a different question from the taxpayer's own other income - that lives in the (30)/(31) grid's 'Other income' columns, see X-26. 433-A asks about household contributors nowhere on its income side.

Recorded as NEW and not as exact, deliberately. 433-A's line 35 totals the taxpayer's income lines; Box D totals a household income that INCLUDES third-party contributions at (32) which 433-A never collects, and a net business income at (36) that differs from 433-A's by the non-cash add-back at X-30. Two totals with the same English name over two different sets of operands. Reusing 433-A's total here is the single largest reuse error available on this form.

THE +3 OFFSET, WHERE IT ACTUALLY HOLDS. Nine of the thirteen offset lines are exact: same question, same monthly figure, printed line number three higher. The other four are X-36, X-37, X-38 and X-39.

Inside the offset band and NOT exact. 433-A asks for 'Vehicle Ownership Costs'; the OIC line asks specifically for 'Vehicle loan and/or lease payment(s)'. The OIC caption is NARROWER - a 433-A ownership figure that included anything beyond the loan or lease payment overstates this line.

Inside the offset band and NOT exact, in the opposite direction to X-36. 433-A asks for 'Current year taxes (Income/FICA)'; the OIC line asks for 'Current monthly taxes (e.g., monthly cost of federal, state, and local tax, personal property tax, etc.)'. The OIC line is BROADER, so a 433-A value is a correct partial answer and an incomplete one.

WHERE THE OFFSET STOPS BEING A FUNCTION. Two 433-A lines land on one OIC line: 47 'Secured Debts (Attach list)' and 49 'Other Expenses (Attach list)' both feed (50) 'Secured debts/Other', whose own caption enumerates 'any loan where you pledged an asset as collateral not previously listed, government guaranteed student loan, employer required retirement or dues'. Adding the two 433-A figures is arithmetic the taxpayer signs for, and the free-text list cell has to be composed from two 433-A attachments.
The last line of the offset band, and exact. The OIC caption pluralises to 'payment(s)' and asks the same monthly question.

TWO COMPONENT DISCLOSURES THE OIC FORM ASKS FOR BESIDE A LINE AND 433-A DOES NOT ASK AT ALL. The FACE AMOUNT of the life insurance policy whose PREMIUM is at (48), two quantities on one printed row differing by three orders of magnitude; and the total state or local tax OWED beside the monthly payment at (51). Neither is a total, neither is an operand of any box, and each is a cell a reader scanning for money cells will find - which is why both are declared not-checkable rather than left out. THIS ENTRY CARRIED A THIRD KEY UNTIL THE RENT REBIND: 40_monthly_rent_payment was classified `new` here, and `new` means "433-A prints nothing like it", which was false - 433-A prints line 37 Housing and Utilities and the OIC rent cell is a component of that same quantity. The false half of a three-key entry derived a form-specific property name for a fact the backbone already held. Split out as X-82.
entries._split_note: Three keys became two here and one at X-82 (the rent rebind). The category is a property of the ENTRY and the deriver reads it off the entry, so an entry covering keys of two different categories cannot name both correctly - which is why the granularity ruling and the rebind are the same commit.

entries.why: Both total the expense lines above them, and the operand SETS differ: 433-A's line 50 adds lines 36-49, fourteen lines including 'Other Expenses'; Box E adds (39)-(51), thirteen lines with no separate other-expenses line and with the two X-38 lines merged. The two totals are over different partitions of the same expenses, so they can legitimately agree and legitimately differ, and neither fact tells you the other is right.

BOX F, Box D minus Box E. 433-A computes no remaining-income figure: it collects income and expenses and stops, and the examiner does the subtraction. On the OIC form the taxpayer does it, and Box F is then multiplied by 12 or 24 on page 7 to produce the future remaining income the offer is built on. Its declared floor is the one no fixture has ever exercised.

entries.a433: 433-A's 'Allowable Expenses' column - 26 cells declared _never_autofill, plus allowed.national_standards_total and allowed.out_of_pocket_health
entries.why: 433-A PRINTS AN IRS-ALLOWED COLUMN BESIDE EVERY EXPENSE LINE AND 433-A(OIC) PRINTS NONE. On 433-A the taxpayer's actual figure and the IRS allowance sit side by side and two of the allowances auto-fill from irs-standards-2026.json. The OIC form has no such column anywhere; instead its printed instruction folds the allowance INTO the taxpayer's own figure on exactly two lines - 'For expenses claimed in boxes (39) and (45) only, you should list the full amount of the allowable standard even if the actual amount you pay is less'. So a 433-A record carries an allowance fact per line that this form has nowhere to put, and on two lines the OIC figure is NOT the taxpayer's actual expense at all. The +3 offset conceals this completely, which is why it is recorded as its own entry.

entries.a433: groups.available_credit (4 slots), groups.payment_processors (2 slots), groups.credit_cards_accepted (3 slots)
entries.why: THREE 433-A TABLES WITH NO OIC COUNTERPART ANYWHERE ON PAGES 1-8. Available credit lines, payment processors, and credit cards accepted by the business. A 433-A record carrying these has facts the OIC filing simply does not ask for. Recorded so a provisioning pass does not read their absence from this file as an oversight. CORRECTED IN PROMPT 37: a fourth table, groups.property_line_20, was listed here and does not belong - see _what_it_got_wrong and _superseded_verbatim. The re-read this entry asked for, against pages 7 and 8, has now happened and confirms the three that remain.

_superseded_verbatim.a433: groups.available_credit (4 slots), groups.payment_processors (2 slots), groups.credit_cards_accepted (3 slots), groups.property_line_20 (2 slots)
_superseded_verbatim.why: FOUR 433-A TABLES WITH NO OIC COUNTERPART ANYWHERE ON PAGES 1-6. Available credit lines, payment processors, credit cards accepted, and the line-20 property table. A 433-A record carrying these has facts the OIC filing simply does not ask for. Recorded so the provisioning pass does not read their absence from this file as an oversight; pages 7-8 are slice 7 and could in principle hold a counterpart, which is why this entry is scoped to pages 1-6 and must be re-read when the map closes.

entries._what_it_got_right: Three of its four tables. 433-A's available-credit lines (16a-16d), payment processors (62a/62b) and credit cards accepted by the business (63a/63b/63c) have NO counterpart anywhere on 433-A(OIC), pages 1-8. Slice 7 authored pages 7 and 8 after this entry was written and the entry told its own reader to re-read it when the map closed; the re-read confirms the three. Pages 7 and 8 are the Box F/G/H offer calculation, Section 9 Other Information and the Section 10 attachment checklist - the nearest things to a counterpart are the safe-deposit box scalars at (10) and the funds-held-in-trust pair, and neither is a credit line, a payment processor or a merchant account.
entries._what_it_got_wrong: The fourth. `groups.property_line_20` DOES have a counterpart, and not on pages 7-8 - on page 4, at (7a), which was already mapped when this entry was written. Four artefacts said so and this one sentence said otherwise: 433aoi.map.json declares groups.7a_other_valuable_items.row_class accepts `personal_property`; asset-row-shapes.json declares `personal_property` is the class 433-A prints at 20a/20b; fields.433a.json binds property_line_20 to irs433_other_personal_property; and X-14 in this same file says the (7a) rows correspond to 433-A's other-valuable-items rows. The consequence if it were believed is a filed one - a preparer reading it drops the taxpayer's personal property from an OIC filing - which is why C-22 was resolved rather than carried again.
entries._how_it_is_now_prevented: adapters/hubspot/reclassify-against-backbone.mjs asserts it mechanically: no `asymmetric-the-other-way` entry may name a 433-A group whose asset class is accepted by a group on this form. It runs at gate step 3 on every form, and it found this entry on its first run before any of the prose above was written.

entries.oic: s8_box_f_for_12_month_multiplier, box_g_future_remaining_income, s8_box_f_for_24_month_multiplier, box_h_future_remaining_income, s8_box_a_plus_box_b, s8_box_g_or_box_h, s8_offer_amount
entries.why: THE WHOLE OF SECTION 8. 433-A collects a financial statement and computes no offer; the minimum-offer calculation - Box F times 12 or 24, plus Box A and Box B - exists only on the OIC form. There is nothing to crosswalk and nothing a 433-A record could supply. Every one of the seven is either computed from cells already on this form or, for the Box-G-or-Box-H cell, chosen from the payment term on Form 656 Section 4. Whether the provisioning pass computes them or stores them is a decision.

Both forms ask "have you filed bankruptcy in the past 7 years" and both draw the same five cells in the same printed order, and the AcroForm leaves are identical down to p1_t38_7[0] being the dismissal date and [1] the discharge date on both. entries.a433: 433-A page 1: c1_6a_[2] Plaintiff, c1_6a_[3] Defendant, p1_t30_6[0] Location of Filing, p1_t31_6[0] Represented by, p1_t32_6[0] Docket/Case No., p1_t35_6[0] Possible Completion Date, p1_t36_6[0] Subject of Suit, amountSuit[0].p1_t34_6[0] Amount of Suit
entries.why: THE SAME EIGHT FACTS, AND THE ONLY FORM WHOSE LEAF NAMES DO NOT MATCH IS THE OIC ONE. 433-A names each cell after what it holds - Location of Filing is p1_t30_6, Amount of Suit is p1_t34_6. 433-A(OIC) names four of them Name_Creditor[0..3], one Date_Final_Payment and one Gross_Receipts, all six of which are wrong (registry L15-L19 and L14). So a crosswalk written from LEAF NAMES on the two forms would pair 433-A’s Location of Filing with nothing and 433-A(OIC)’s Name_Creditor[0] with a lender cell on page 3. The facts are exact; the names are the trap.

entries.why: Both forms ask "Are you currently incarcerated" and both provide one cell for the inmate number. The OIC form additionally names its subform currentlyIncarcerated[0], which 433-A does not - the only place on either form where the container name states the question. CAUTION ON THE LEAF p2_t50_8: on 433-A that leaf is "Do you have dual citizenship" at [0] and "Are you currently incarcerated" at [1]; on 433-A(OIC) the same leaf holds "Dates lived abroad: From". One leaf name, three different questions across two forms.

IDENTICAL LEAF NAMES AND IDENTICAL FACTS. Even the anonymous-subform nesting is the same shape: the anticipated-amount cell is one level deeper than its row-mates on BOTH forms - #subform[3] on 433-A, #subform[8] on 433-A(OIC). 433-A declares /MaxLen 2 on the EIN cell and /MaxLen 12 on the amount; 433-A(OIC) declares neither.

entries.a433: 433-A page 2: the trustee Yes/No pair, p2_t00_9b[0] and p1-t02_9b[0]
entries.why: Identical leaf names and identical facts. NOTE that on both forms the leaf p2_t00_9b holds the NAME OF THE TRUST and not the question, which the 433-A label file misreports as the question text - a correlation artefact on both forms rather than a difference between them.

entries.a433: 433-A page 2: c1_10_[0]/[1], p1_t41_10[0] Location, p1-t43_10[0] Contents, value[0].p1-t42_10[0] Value
entries.why: IDENTICAL, INCLUDING THE DEFECT. The 41 / 43 / 42 suffix inversion recorded as [L21] on 433-A(OIC) is present on 433-A TOO, in the same three columns and the same order - Location is 41, Contents is 43, Value is 42 on both. So the inversion is not an OIC quirk: it is inherited from the shared source, and 433-B and 433-B(OIC) should be read for it before their safe-deposit rows are bound. 433-A wraps its Value cell in a subform named value[0] and 433-A(OIC) does not, which means an author reading 433-A would be warned by that subform name and an author reading the OIC form would not.

IDENTICAL LEAF NAMES, IDENTICAL FACTS, AND THE SAME NESTING ANOMALY: the value-at-time-of-transfer cell is nested one level deeper than its three row-mates on BOTH forms. 433-A declares /MaxLen 12 on the value and 8 on the date; the OIC form declares neither.

entries.a433: 433-A page 2: c1_8_[0]/[1] and the two date cells p2_t50_8b[0] / p2_t51_8b[0]
entries.why: The same question and the same two dates. The leaf names differ by one character - 433-A appends "b" (p2_t50_8b) where the OIC form does not (p2_t50_8) - and that single character is the difference between the right cell and the dual-citizenship cell on 433-A. A crosswalk matching leaves by prefix would collide here.

THE IRS-LITIGATION QUESTION IS NEW. 433-A asks about litigation generally and asks nothing about litigation involving the IRS or the United States. There is no 433-A cell for it and no 433-A value that partly answers it - a "yes" to the general litigation question says nothing about who the other party was.

NEW. 433-A carries the words "foreign countries or jurisdictions" inside three of its own questions - the beneficiary, trustee and safe-deposit ones - but asks no separate question about assets or real property held outside the U.S. and provides no cell for a description of them. Do not source this from 433-A line 19 real property: that line asks for property wherever it is and its answers are already bound at (5a)/(5b) here.

NEW. 433-A asks whether the taxpayer is a beneficiary of a trust and whether they are a trustee of one, and never asks whether a third party is holding funds for them. A record built from 433-A has no value for this and no near-miss to be tempted by.

Nothing in a 433-A record could populate them and nothing in this engine can confirm one; whether they are driven from the intake at all is carried open as C-18.

entries.a433: (nothing — 433-A carries no field whose name matches /sign/i at all, on any page)
entries.why: RECORDED SO THE PROVISIONING PASS DOES NOT CREATE A PROPERTY FOR IT. entries.a433: 433-A page 2: p2_t50_8[0], "Do you have dual citizenship", with its own Yes/No pair
entries.why: RECORDED BECAUSE A ONE-DIRECTIONAL CROSSWALK HIDES IT. 433-A asks about dual citizenship and 433-A(OIC) does not, so a taxpayer moving from a 433-A filing to an OIC filing drops that fact. It is listed here for the same reason the two earlier asymmetric entries are: a fact with nowhere to go is a fact the OIC filing loses, and the loss should be a decision rather than an omission. The leaf p2_t50_8 is ALSO the trap named in X-48 - on the OIC form it holds a date.
The OIC form asks "If married, date of marriage" beside its marital-status boxes. 433-A asks marital status and never a date. Nothing to crosswalk.
Marital status, two printed options on both forms and the same two: Unmarried and Married. The printed ORDER differs and the option SET does not.

"Do you: Own your home / Rent / Other (specify e.g., share rent, live with relative, etc.)" with its write-in cell. 433-A asks no housing question anywhere - it collects a home address and a housing-and-utilities EXPENSE and never asks the tenure. Nothing to crosswalk.

"If you were married and lived in AZ, CA, ID, LA, NM, NV, TX, WA or WI within the last ten years check here". A community-property-state question 433-A does not ask. It is a lone check-here box, so the negative answer is the box left blank.
Pay period for taxpayer and spouse, four printed options on both forms and the same four: weekly, bi-weekly, monthly, other.

READ THE PRINTED QUESTION, NOT THE KEY. Section 2 asks "Do you have an ownership interest in this business" and "Does your spouse have an ownership interest in this business" - THIS business being the EMPLOYER named in the same section, each answer carrying "(also complete and submit Form 433-B)". 433-A asks nothing about owning an interest in your own employer. Its item-3 question, "Do you or your spouse have any interest in a business", is about businesses generally and is the counterpart of the OIC form Section 4 question at s4_other_business_interests (X-73), not of these. Binding either of these to irs433_business_interest would answer a question about the employer with an answer about some other company.

THE PRINTED $1,000. The OIC line reads "Add lines (1a) through (1c) minus ($1,000) =" and 433-A line 13e reads "Total Cash (Add lines 13a, 13b, 13c, 13d and amounts from any attachments)" with no deduction of any kind. A 433-A total copied here overstates the OIC figure by exactly $1,000, and every printed total on the page still reconciles. Same shape as the quick-sale discount at X-07: the captions correspond and the arithmetic does not.

The lone "check here" box that opens the (2c) digital-asset block, and the (2c) identity total beneath it. 433-A prints neither: it has no check-here box for digital assets, and its line 15e is a four-row EQUITY total rather than one asset dollar equivalent. RECORDED ALSO AS A DISAGREEMENT: the identical pair on page 4 - 8c_digital_asset_held and 8c_total_digital_assets - falls inside the "8c_* digital-asset block" glob X-18 declares and is therefore classified different-shape, while these two are classified new. Two structurally identical constructs, two categories, because one entry globbed and the other enumerated. Carried as C-21. It changes neither naming outcome; both are form-specific.

433-A prints NO investments total. It totals cash at 13e, digital assets at 15e, available credit at 16e, life insurance at 17f, real property at 18d, vehicles at 19d and personal property at 20c, and its line 14 investments table has no total cell at all. The OIC (2) total also ABSORBS the digital-asset figure at (2c), so the nearest 433-A total, 15e, is an operand of this one rather than a counterpart to it.

One printed policy row against 433-A three, with the OIC attachment block split into a total and a separate loan-balance cell whose difference is carried at (4b). The CONTAINER differs and the arithmetic does not: both totals are cash value minus loan balance over every policy, and neither form prints a quick-sale discount on life insurance. (4b) itself has no 433-A cell - 433-A folds attachment amounts into 17f without printing a cell for them.

The OIC form prints a vehicle attachment roll-up line and 433-A prints none: 433-A line 19d says "and amounts from any attachments" inside the total caption and gives the attachment no cell of its own. Note the leaf name here is a lie - Enter_Allowance[0], registry L10 - so this line could not have been crosswalked by name in either direction.

THE PRINTED $11,980. The OIC line reads "Add lines (7a) through (7c) minus IRS deduction of $11,980 =" and 433-A line 20c reads "Total Equity (Add lines 20a, 20b and amounts from any attachments)". Two differences, either alone disqualifying reuse: the printed IRS deduction, and the quick-sale discount already carried on the rows that feed it. Same shape as X-66.
Average gross monthly payroll for the self-employed business. Same fact, same question, different section number.

entries.oic: s4_other_business_percentage_ownership, s4_other_business_title, s4_other_business_name, s4_other_business_type_other, s4_other_business_interests, s4_other_business_type
entries.why: THE OTHER-BUSINESS BLOCK, AND ITS COUNTERPART IS 433-A ITEM 3 - not 433-A Section 5. The OIC form asks "Do you or your spouse have any other business interests? Include any interest in an LLC, LLP, corporation, partnership, etc." and 433-A item 3 asks "Do you or your spouse have any interest in a business", both followed by percentage of ownership, title, business name and a four-option business type with a write-in. Six facts, same questions, same option sets. The OIC form asks three further cells in the same block that 433-A does not - see X-74.

Address, telephone and EIN for the OTHER business. 433-A item 3 asks for none of the three: it names the business and its type and stops, and its own EIN cell at line 54 belongs to the SELF-EMPLOYED business in Section 5, which on this form is s4_business_ein (X-16). Reusing line 54 here would put the taxpayer own business EIN against a company they merely hold an interest in.
"Is your business a sole proprietorship" against 433-A "Is your business a sole proprietorship (filing Schedule C)?". The OIC page draws no question mark and 433-A does; the question is the same one.

The OIC (8) total is "Add lines (8a) through (8d)" and (8c) is the BUSINESS DIGITAL ASSET dollar equivalent. So this total sums business bank balances AND business digital assets AND the attachment roll-up, where 433-A line 65c sums business bank balances only and puts every digital asset - business or personal - in its own line 15. The leaf name understates it the same way the page does, which is why the registry carries it as P01 page_imprecise rather than as a lie.
The accounting period the business income and expense figures cover. Same two cells, same question, on both forms.

ONE OIC LINE OVER TWO 433-A LINES. The OIC caption is "Vehicle costs" with "(gas, oil, repairs, maintenance)" printed beside it at y 163.1; 433-A prints "Vehicle Gasoline/Oil" at 84 and "Repairs and Maintenance" at 85 as separate lines. Binding this to 84 alone drops repairs and maintenance from a business expense figure on a statement signed under penalty of perjury, and line (29) still reconciles. Adding the two is arithmetic the taxpayer signs for, which is what this category means. Found while deriving property names; X-23 had it inside its offset claim.

"Secured debts" with "(not credit cards)" printed beside it, as a BUSINESS expense line. 433-A business expense block, lines 78-88, prints no secured-debt line at all. Do not source it from 433-A line 47 "Secured Debts (Attach list)": that line is in 433-A PERSONAL living-expense block and is already claimed by X-38 for the OIC personal line (50). One of the two would be answering for the wrong section.

entries.a433: 433-A lines 72-76: 72_bizinc_cash_receipts_not_in_68_to_71 and the four Other Income description/amount pairs at 73-76
entries.why: ONE OIC CELL OVER FIVE 433-A CELLS. 433-A prints "Cash Receipts not included in lines 68-71" at 72 and four further "Other Income (Specify below)" description/amount pairs at 73-76; the OIC form prints one plain "Other income" cell at (16) with no description cell beside it. Every individual fact crosswalks and no LINE does, and the OIC form has nowhere to put the four descriptions.

Both total the expense lines above them and the operand SETS differ, because the OIC block carries a secured-debts line (27) that 433-A does not - see X-79. The two totals can legitimately agree and legitimately differ, and nothing on either page says which. Same reasoning as X-41 on the household-expense side.

THE RENT COMPONENT INSIDE THE OIC HOUSING FIGURE, AND THE FACT THE BACKBONE ALREADY HELD. 433-A prints ONE line 37, "Housing and Utilities", and X-35 already classifies the OIC's own (40) housing total as `exact` against it. Beside that total the OIC form prints a monthly rent cell - one PART of the same quantity, which is precisely same-fact-different-decomposition and not `new`. 433-F decomposes the same quantity further still, into five printed rows of which Rent is the first, and holds that row as the live backbone property `irs433_exp_rent`. THIS IS C-23'S OWN INSTANCE: the classification vocabulary is defined relative to 433-A, `irs433_exp_rent` was contributed by 433-F, and no entry in a 433-A-relative file could see it. The mechanical surfacing came from adapters/hubspot/reclassify-against-backbone.mjs, whose widened target compares against every irs433_ property rather than against one predecessor form, and which ruled this pair same-fact and declined to rebind because which property a filed cell reads from is permanent state. It is rebound HERE, and the reason it can be is that there is no cheaper moment and there never will be one again: the only record that ever held either value was the synthetic probe, which was deleted, so ZERO LIVE RECORDS carry the orphaned property. Leaving it would mean one taxpayer's rent living in two properties that can diverge - the exact failure a shared backbone exists to prevent - and it would cost a slot against a ceiling that cannot be walked back.

_tally._why: Derived from entries[] by adapters/pdf/count-sweep.mjs [S-25], never retyped. A hand-kept tally beside a list is how 'eleven' survived three slices when the honest figure was ten.
_tally._the_typed_tally_was_wrong_on_three_cate: AUTHORED BY HAND AS 16 exact / 8 different-shape / 8 new, DERIVED AS 14 / 7 / 11. Corrected to the derived figures before this file was ever committed. Left recorded because it is the fourth time in this repo a hand-kept count beside its own list has drifted, and the first time the drift was caught in the same minute it was written - by [S-25], which existed before the file did.
_tally._slice_7: Slice 7 added fifteen entries covering pages 7 and 8. NINE ARE `exact` AND THAT IS THE FINDING: 433-A(OIC) Section 9 and 433-A’s "Other Information" block are the same questions in the same order under the same AcroForm leaf names, index for index, including two nesting anomalies and one suffix inversion that are present on BOTH forms. 62 of the 334 distinct leaf names on 433-A(OIC) also appear on 433-A, and this block is where most of them are. The shared lineage is real and it is also where the sharpest traps live: p2_t50_8 names three different questions across the two forms, p2_t50_8b differs from p2_t50_8 by one character and by one question, and the six litigation cells are named correctly on 433-A and wrongly on 433-A(OIC).
_tally._slice_8: The naming pass added twenty-two entries and corrected three. Every added entry covers keys the completeness blanket claimed were already covered - see _the_completeness_blanket_was_false_when_it_was_written. The category mix of the additions is the finding in miniature: nine exact facts 433-A asks identically and nobody had crosswalked, and four totals carrying a printed constant or an absorbed operand that 433-A does not carry.

_what_this_file_does_not_say: IT DOES NOT SAY WHICH HUBSPOT PROPERTY FEEDS ANYTHING. An `exact` classification means a 433-A value needs no transformation to become the OIC value; it does NOT mean a property already exists, that it is the right property, or that reuse is approved. The provisioning pass reads these categories to know WHICH DECISIONS IT HAS TO MAKE - every entry that is not `exact` is a decision - and makes them there.
_the_reading_that_matters: SEVEN OF THE FORTY-FOUR ENTRIES ARE different-arithmetic-same-name, AND THOSE ARE THE FILE'S REASON TO EXIST. Each is a pair the captions invite you to reuse and the arithmetic forbids: the quick-sale discount on four asset classes, the non-cash add-back at (36), the narrowed vehicle line at (41), and the two household totals at Box E. Every one of them produces a filed statement whose printed totals all reconcile and whose offer is wrong.
_covers_slices_superseded_verbatim: 1-7, pages 1-8. THE CLASSIFICATION IS COMPLETE for 433-A(OIC): every bound key on the form is covered by an entry.
_the_completeness_blanket_was_false_when: IT READ: "1-7, pages 1-8. THE CLASSIFICATION IS COMPLETE for 433-A(OIC): every bound key on the form is covered by an entry." IT WAS NOT. Thirty-one of the 238 input keys 433aoi.map.json declares were named by no entry, verbatim or by any glob, range or counted phrase any entry states - among them the marital-status, pay-period and accounting-period cells 433-A asks identically, the whole other-business block, and FOUR TOTALS: (1) minus a printed $1,000, (7) minus a printed $11,980, (8) absorbing business digital assets 433-A puts elsewhere, and (2) with no 433-A counterpart at all. The blanket was true of 207 of 238 keys and false of 31, which is the shape of defect this file was opened to catch. Nothing checked it because the check did not exist: the sweep counted ENTRIES, and no tool had ever compared the entries against the KEY SPACE. That comparison is now assertion A1 in derive-names-433aoi.mjs and it runs before any property is created.
_what_the_naming_pass_changed: THREE CORRECTIONS AND TWENTY-TWO ADDITIONS, all found by deriving a HubSpot property name for every bound key and asserting the result. X-17 was new and is exact - 433-A line 57 is a business-website cell, so the derived name would have been a permanent duplicate of irs433_business_website. X-22 claimed five identically-asked income sources and had four. X-23 claimed eleven identically-asked expense lines plus a total and had nine. Each keeps its superseded text verbatim under _superseded_verbatim, with what it got right and what it got wrong.
_compared_against_the_backbone: AGAINST 433-A ALONE IS NOW A DECLARED NARROWNESS RATHER THAN AN IMPLIED ONE. `against` above still records the predecessor this file was authored from, and every entry now also carries `compared_against`, DERIVED from which forms' artefacts actually hold the facts that entry's keys bind. The backbone is not 433-A: 433-F contributed 90 of the live irs433_* names, so a fact 433-F named and 433-A does not print was invisible to this file by construction and came out classified `new`. adapters/hubspot/reclassify-against-backbone.mjs widens the target to the live backbone plus every mapped form, reports every category change, and STOPS on a `new`-classified key that shares a fact with a backbone name another form contributed unless that candidate carries a ruling. See C-23, which is what this construct was built for and which it has not closed.
_granularity_is_declared_per_entry: EVERY ENTRY CARRIES `granularity`, DERIVED FROM HOW IT NAMES ITS KEYS. `enumerated` means it spells each key out - the narrowest claim, and the only one that says its author looked at the cell. `glob` means it wrote a prefix and swept in whatever matched. `derived-counterpart` means it named N keys and said 'and the five spouse counterparts'. `names-no-key-on-this-form` is what an `asymmetric-the-other-way` entry correctly has. A category is only comparable across entries at a stated granularity, and this is the statement. Where two entries describe the same printed construct at two granularities the reclassifier reports the pair and requires a declared reason - today exactly one such pair exists, X-09 against X-18, which is C-21.
